criteria.no: Compliance rests on a subjective quality, a label or mode the statement never defines, or an expected output, approval, or standard with no identified record.
criteria.unclear: A concrete outcome is partly named, but it cannot be told what to inspect even though nothing is undefined or unrecorded.
criteria.yes: The statement names a concrete behavior, output, file, path, value, prohibited content, or identified record whose presence or absence can be checked.

observable.instructions: Bundled duties do not matter here: a statement with several duties is observable when each duty's outcome is concrete. Could a reviewer decide pass or fail for each outcome of `anchor.statement` by inspecting a concrete behavior, output, file, path, value, command result, or recorded artifact? A mode, profile, or label is inspectable only when the statement itself defines it (for example 'offline mode (when --offline is set)'); a name the statement never defines (such as Mode K or R7) gives nothing to inspect. A reference to an expected output, approval, or standard is inspectable only when the statement identifies where it is recorded (a named file, path, or list); 'the expected output' or 'after the owner signs off' with no identified record gives nothing to inspect. A subjective quality (robust, clean) gives nothing to inspect. Judge every part the outcome depends on, such as its destination, target, mode, or tier: if any such part is a name the statement never defines, nothing settles compliance, even when the other parts name concrete files or paths. Bundled duties, added details, and informal wording do not matter here.

anchor.statement: A schema migration may run only when its migration ID is listed in docs/approvals/migrations.md.
anchor.quote: migrations only run once their ID is listed in docs/approvals/migrations.md
